coordinates: SIMBAD basic table, ICRS J2000, degrees
angular_sizes: SIMBAD galdim, arcminutes; omitted where SIMBAD has no value
note: Every distance is a published measurement with its method and reference recorded. Images are real telescope data, not renders.

objects.name: Pleiades
objects.blurb: A cluster young enough that its stars still drift through the dust they formed from. The blue haze is reflected starlight.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of cluster members, 7.364 mas
objects.image_credit: NASA, ESA, AURA/Caltech, Palomar Observatory The science team consists of: D. Soderblom and E. Nelan (STScI), F. Benedict and B. Arthur (U. Texas), and B. Jones (Lick Obs.)

objects.name: Helix Nebula
objects.blurb: One of the nearest planetary nebulae, which is why it looks so large. The knots around the inner edge are each about the size of our solar system.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of the central star, 5.012 mas
objects.image_credit: The HST data are from proposal 9700. Processed images may be obtained from the Helix MAST web site. The Hubble Helix Team includes M. Meixner, H.E. Bond, G. Chapman (STScI), Y.-H. Chu (U. Illinois, Ur

objects.name: Dumbbell Nebula
objects.blurb: The first planetary nebula ever found, by Messier in 1764, long before anyone knew what it was.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of the central star, 2.570 mas

objects.name: Orion Nebula
objects.blurb: The closest region of massive star formation. Four thousand young stars sit inside it, and the four hottest are burning the cavity you are looking into.
objects.image_credit: NASA, ESA, M. Robberto (Space Telescope Science Institute/ESA) and the Hubble Space Telescope Orion Treasury Project Team

objects.name: Horsehead Nebula
objects.blurb: A column of opaque dust in front of a glowing background. You are seeing the shape of what blocks the light, not the light.
objects.dist_method: distance to the parent Orion B molecular cloud
objects.dist_ref: Orion B cloud distance, about 420 pc
objects.caveat: The Horsehead is a silhouette in a cloud; the distance is the cloud's, not a direct measurement of the pillar.

objects.name: Veil Nebula
objects.blurb: A supernova shock wave still expanding after roughly ten thousand years, now spread across six times the width of the full Moon.
objects.dist_method: Gaia distances to stars bracketing the shell

objects.name: Ring Nebula
objects.blurb: Not a ring but a barrel seen down its axis. The dark centre is the hole through the middle.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of the central star, 1.270 mas
objects.image_credit: NASA, ESA, C.R. Robert O’Dell (Vanderbilt University), G.J. Ferland (University of Kentucky), W.J. Henney and M. Peimbert (National Autonomous University of Mexico) Credit for Large Binocular Telescop

objects.name: North America Nebula
objects.blurb: An emission nebula whose outline happens to resemble a continent. The resemblance is a coincidence of perspective.
objects.dist_ref: Zucker et al. 2020, A&A 633, A51 — about 795 pc

objects.name: Lagoon Nebula
objects.blurb: A star nursery bright enough to see without a telescope from a dark site, split by a dust lane that gives it its name.
objects.dist_ref: Damiani et al. 2019, A&A 623, A25 — 1.25 kpc

objects.name: Trifid Nebula
objects.blurb: Three kinds of nebula at once: emission, reflection, and the dark lanes that cut it into three.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of the ionising cluster, 0.790 mas
objects.image_credit: International Gemini Observatory/Ingrid Braul, Southlands Elementary, Vancouver BC

objects.name: Cat's Eye Nebula
objects.blurb: A dying sun-like star shedding its outer layers in concentric shells about every 1,500 years. The rings are a record of that rhythm.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of the central star, 0.732 mas
objects.caveat: A single-star parallax at 1.4 kpc carries a real uncertainty; published distances for this nebula range from about 1.0 to 1.5 kpc.

objects.name: Pillars of Creation
objects.blurb: Columns of cold molecular dust being eaten away from the outside by ultraviolet light from the cluster above them. They are shrinking, not growing.
objects.dist_method: Gaia parallax of the ionising cluster NGC 6611, 0.566 mas
objects.image_credit: SCIENCE: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; IMAGE PROCESSING: Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Anton M. Koekemoer (STScI), Alyssa Pagan (STScI)
objects.caveat: The parallax belongs to the cluster lighting the pillars, not to the dust itself.

objects.name: Crab Nebula
objects.blurb: The wreckage of a star seen exploding by Chinese astronomers in 1054 CE. A neutron star at the centre spins thirty times a second.
objects.image_credit: NASA , ESA , J. Hester and A. Loll (Arizona State University)
objects.caveat: Expansion distances are model-dependent; this one is not a parallax.

objects.name: Carina Nebula
objects.blurb: A star-forming complex far larger and more violent than Orion, holding Eta Carinae — a star that may already be dead.
objects.dist_method: parallax of the ionising cluster Trumpler 16, 0.380 mas

objects.name: Omega Centauri
objects.blurb: Ten million stars bound into a sphere. It may be the stripped core of a small galaxy the Milky Way swallowed.

objects.name: Tarantula Nebula
objects.blurb: The most active star-forming region known in the Local Group — and it is not even in our galaxy.
objects.dist_method: distance to the Large Magellanic Cloud
objects.image_credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Webb ERO Production Team
objects.anchor_note: Anchored to the Large Magellanic Cloud row in Cosmicflows-3, which is its host galaxy.
objects.caveat: The nebula's distance is inherited from its host galaxy.

objects.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
objects.blurb: A face-on spiral being pulled out of shape by the smaller galaxy at the end of one arm.
objects.dist_method: Cosmicflows-3 measured distance to NGC 5195, 7.31 Mpc
objects.anchor_note: Anchored to the Cosmicflows-3 row for NGC 5195, the interacting companion.
objects.caveat: CF3 lists the companion NGC 5195; the pair shares a distance to within its own uncertainty.

objects.name: Sombrero Galaxy
objects.blurb: An edge-on spiral with a dust lane sharp enough to look drawn, wrapped around an unusually large bulge.
objects.dist_ref: Tully et al. 2016, AJ 152, 50 — the catalogue this project already ships
objects.image_credit: NASA/ESA and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)
